title: Two-step word problems: the `word-work` two-step layouts (columns, frames, letter equation, estimate) and the new two-step bar model

template.also: A COPY on the live `word-work` drawing (owner ruling 2026-09-25: one cell type for every whole-number story; owned by the visual-quality lane, ask the lead before changing it): its two-step `columns` blocks (Step 1 | Step 2, each with its own sign row; tellTwoStep retells the story) and its `frames` layout (wpFrames; msLetter = one equation with n; msCheck = the estimate rows). ONE NEW PART: the two-step bar model (a new graphic-library entry beside graphics/part-whole-bar.js; today wpBar draws nothing on a two-step story, `bar: !!o.bar && steps.length === 1`), so the first build of that part runs at medium. Generator: gen-algebraic.js `multi_step_word` (msOps / msChoose blocks and the four + / − archetypes); post-step js/modules/word-work.js (TWO_STEP); provider js/modules/sheet/providers/word-work.js (moves, ms-* wrong answers, iCan); detailed lesson js/modules/lessons/detailed/g3-oa8-two-step-wp.js. screen-cell.js / wordWorkTwin draw the same cell on the practice card, online worksheet and quiz

summary: Seven skills on one drawing: algebra:multi_step_word_plain (the host) and its twin multi_step_word, plus the five presets of detailed lesson 7 (two_step_mult_div_first {msOps: multdiv}, two_step_add_then_mult {addmult}, two_step_add_then_div {adddiv}, two_step_letter_equation {multdiv, msLetter}, two_step_estimate_check {msCheck}). A story of at most 5 lines (P-WP-17), then the work: two titled step columns (Step 1 | Step 2, a sign row each, column boxes; the Step 1 answer carried into Step 2) or, faded, one number sentence a step (frames); the letter preset writes ONE equation with n and then n; the estimate preset adds the rounded estimate and a Yes / No 'is my answer close?'. The two-step bar model (new) is drawn on the teaching pages and is the wpBar option on practice pages. Paper, key and the three screen hosts are one drawing.
teaches: 3.OA.D.8 (two-step word problems with the four operations; represent them with an equation with a letter for the unknown; assess the answer by mental computation and estimation, rounding), 2.OA.A.1 (+ and − within 100, one- and two-step), 4.OA.A.3 (multistep with whole numbers; the remainder part is the division family's remainder_interpret, not this card). EE M.EE.3.OA.7 (the repo tag; lesson 7 Q1: the owner sheet's M.EE.3.OA.8 quotes M.EE.3.OA.7's text), M.EE.4.OA.3. BUILD lessons served (data/curriculum/ccss-build-lessons.json): #7 G3 W06 'Two-step word problems with the four operations' (3.OA.D.8; detailed lesson g3-oa8-two-step-wp, chunks x-first and ÷-first; follow-on lessons = the presets add-first, letter, estimate); #17 G2 W09 'Solve two-step word problems identifying both operations' (2.OA.A.1; G2-Y3.B2 BUILD: multi_step_word, + / − within 100, a sign row per step); related #39 G3 W17 'add and subtraction word problems within 1,000 using bar models' (3.NBT.A.2 + 3.OA.D.8: the two-step bar model is reused; its main skills are the add / sub story families) and #24 G4 W11 (4.OA.A.3 remainders: division family).
research: Reached: IXL public skill list (ixl.com/math/word-problems, grade 3 names only: 'Two-step addition and subtraction word problems', 'Two-step multiplication and division word problems', 'Two-step word problems: represent and solve using strip models', 'Two-step mixed operation word problems', 'Two-step word problems: identify reasonable answers', 'Write equations with unknown numbers to represent word problems'); MathWorksheets4Kids public pages (word-problems.php, equation-word-problems.php: two-step EQUATION word problems are grade 6+, write the equation then solve, plus an MCQ 'match the equation' set; the grade 3-4 two-step pages were not found publicly: /two-step.php and /multi-step-word-problems.php are 404; no login this round - a WebFetch cannot hold a session); K5 Learning grade-3 word problems (mixed word problems - mental math / column math / simpler form; mixed + / −; mixed x / ÷; no titled two-step set); Math-Drills 403 (unreachable). Repo research reused: design/lesson-planner/lessons/g3-oa8-two-step-wp/RESEARCH.md (Achieve the Core 3.OA.D.8 mini-assessment, Super Teacher Worksheets 3.OA.8, TES two-step solvers, CazoomMaths with / without clues, Have Fun Teaching match-the-equation). Sequence taken (not pacing): + / − two-step -> x or ÷ first then + / − -> + / − first then x / ÷ (brackets) -> equation with a letter -> reasonable answers by rounding; strip (bar) models as the representation. Where our standards override the sites: no clue text or keyword bolding (P-21), black and white, one story a cell, at most 4 a page, a sign row per step instead of one 'which operation' choice, the A-D choice only as the teacher's msChoose response mode.
problemTypes: addsub (host default, G2 2.OA.A.1): + / − then + / − in the four orders (forms: add then take away, take away then add, add twice, take away twice); column boxes, a sign row per step; numbers to the band

mult / div / multdiv (= preset two_step_mult_div_first, lesson 7 chunks a / b): a x or ÷ fact within 10 x 10 whose answer feeds a + or − step ('5 bags of 9, 13 more'; '12 shared by 3, each gets 6 more')
addmult (= preset two_step_add_then_mult): a + or − step first, then x ('each bag has 6 red and 3 blue; 2 bags'): brackets (6 + 3) x 2
adddiv (= preset two_step_add_then_div): + or − first, then ÷ ('17, keeps 5, shares the rest among 6'): (17 − 5) ÷ 6
msLetter (= preset two_step_letter_equation): the whole story as ONE equation with n ('5 x 9 + 13 = n', brackets when + / − comes first), then 'n = [ ]'
msCheck (= preset two_step_estimate_check): work the two steps, round each story number to the nearest ten, write the estimate, ring Yes / No 'is my answer close to the estimate?'
msChoose (response mode, no preset; lesson 7 r3): x / ÷ first then take away; check one of four answers A-D (the answer and the three two-step errors)
wpFrames (fade): one number sentence a step 'Step 1: [ ] ( ) [ ] = [ ]' instead of the column boxes - the exit slip / Prerequisite Check form
wpBar (NEW drawing, PROPOSED Q4): the two-step bar model under the story - Step 1 bar (equal groups or part-whole), Step 2 bar whose whole or part is the Step 1 answer; labels blank
progression: 1 G2: add then take away, answers to 30 (band 30), two step columns with sign rows, bar model on the teaching pages -> 2 all four + / − orders mixed (forms) -> 3 answers to 50 -> 4 answers to 100 (one change a step: the order kind OR the number size)

5 G3: x first then + / − (msOps mult) -> 6 ÷ first (div) -> 7 x or ÷ first mixed (multdiv = two_step_mult_div_first) -> 8 + / − first then x (addmult) -> 9 + / − first then ÷ (adddiv) -> 10 one equation with a letter, x / ÷ first (two_step_letter_equation) -> 11 the letter with brackets (msLetter + addmult / adddiv) -> 12 estimate to check (two_step_estimate_check, + / − stories to 100)

Fade within each step (P-1: the scaffold changes alone, never with the content): bar model drawn (teaching pages) -> bar off, column boxes (independent) -> frames (wpFrames: the pupil still produces every number and sign); the printed middle question (P-WP-11 v1, PROPOSED Q6) and the grey Step 1 sign trace are hints that go first; the two titled step columns, the sign rows, the answer row with its unit bank are structural and stay
G4 4.OA.A.3 continues on the division family (remainder_interpret) and on the build entry multi_step_four_ops (G4-Y5.B3, G5-Y6.B2 parts not on this card)

drawing.sizes: Story at the cell-text size + 2 (13 / 15 / 17 pt S / M / L; WDS row 'Cell text the pupil must read' 11 / 13 / 15 + 2, P-WP-17 one sentence a line, at most 5 lines); work digits at the working digit size (ctx.metrics digitPt; 16 / 22 / 28 pt); work and answer boxes the answer-area boxes 14 x 11 / 14.3 x 13 / 17 x 15 mm (2 digits; wider by blankWidth for 3), the answer box 1.5 pt, working boxes 1 pt, sign circles 9 / 11 / 13 mm 1 pt; the two step columns split by a 1.5 pt vertical rule (WDS 11.9 Two-step), each headed 'Step 1' / 'Step 2' at text size bold. Two-step bar model (new): bars 10 / 12 / 14 mm tall, 1.5 pt outline (RP-70), schematic and fixed (RP-72: equal groups = n equal segments, at most 6 drawn; part-whole = 60 / 40), label boxes 0.75 pt writing places, exactly one '?' unknown per bar (LS-3), never dashed.
notes: Answer slots (VQ-2 one answer place per answer): columns - ONE graded slot, the Step 2 bottom row (the quotient row of ÷) in heavier boxes, the unit line beside it with a three-word bank (P-TH-1); the Step 1 result, both sign rows and every work box are working places (data-ws-graded=0 on paper, input.mq-wwork with data-mq-expect on screen, marked as typed, never scored). frames - the last step's result box graded, the unit word PRINTED. letter (PROPOSED Q7) - TWO graded answers: the equation (both sign circles and the three number boxes, one 'equation' answer) and n. estimate (PROPOSED Q8) - two graded answers: the answer and the estimate; the Yes / No ring is ungraded reflection (the key rings it). msChoose - one graded choice A-D (ring on paper, buttons on screen).

Key (AK-1): the same cell finished - both signs ringed, every number, the Step 1 result, the answer and its unit; letter: the equation and n; estimate: the rounded numbers, the estimate, Yes ringed; bar model: every label written.

Two-step bar model payload (new, PROPOSED Q4): {bar2: {s1: {kind: 'groups'|'whole', parts, whole}, s2: {kind: 'whole'|'compare', a, b, whole}, carry: 'whole'|'part'}}; the Step 1 bar's total box and the Step 2 bar's carried box are joined by a 0.75 pt arrow labelled 'Step 1 answer' at zone-label size; never proportional, so the length never shows which number is bigger.

Screen twin (wordWorkTwin): the same drawing in --mq-k2 px, the step columns stacked on a phone card (Step 1 above Step 2, no vertical rule), sign rows as 44 px buttons, work boxes typed with live marks, the answer the host's own digit boxes (data-mq-cell). No paper production turns into a choice on screen (msChoose is a choice on both).

Capacity (PROPOSED Q9, measured at build by ws-options-verify --render; content never shrinks): columns one across, S 3 / M 2 / L 2 a page; frames S 4 / M 4 / L 2; letter and estimate frames S 4 / M 3 / L 2; with the bar model (adds a drawing; the bar above the column work) S 2 / M 1 / L 1 (lead ruling R1 2026-11-13 (a): measured S 2 / M 1 / L 1; a bar beside the column work cannot reach M 2 (probe, widest of 200 stories at M: bar across 132.3 x 29.8 mm, stacked 62.5 x 61.6 mm, the two step columns 107 mm wide and 53.7 mm tall, the story 27.5 mm - side by side needs 181-247 mm of a 174 mm row and a 102 mm cell, over 93 mm); M holds 1 as a ruled pin and the one-story practice page must not stretch its row (a role change, lf-roles); check ws-two-step --print CAP-BAND); msChoose S 4 / M 4 / L 2. WDS 12.1: 'Word problem v2 (faded)' 2 a page, plain rows 4 / 3 / 3 - research fits 6-10, we do not.

'Within N' bounds the ANSWER and every computed number (PROPOSED Q2): band N caps the Step 1 result and the answer (the sum, the number taken from, the product, the dividend); story numbers are below it. With no band the Max Number is that cap. x / ÷ first: a fixed facts domain (factors 2-6 by 2-9, dividend <= 54), Step 2 number 2-20, answer 1-100, the Max Number does not apply. + / − first then x / ÷: the bracket sum 4-10 (x) or a multiple of the divisor <= 54 (÷), answer <= 60 / <= 9.

Item guards (all msOps): the Step 2 number is no Step 1 number; the answer is no story number and not the Step 1 answer (today ~0.7 % of addsub items break this: build fixes); Step 2 never cancels Step 1; no remainders; a take-away never leaves 0.

Lesson routine (BUILD #7, lesson 7 data): Read it. What do I find first? / Step 1: groups or share. x or ÷. / Step 2: use my Step 1 answer. / Write the answer and the unit. Chants 'First the groups. Then the change.' (chunk a) and 'First the share. Then the change.' (chunk b). Follow-on lessons (presets): add first - 'Step 1: put them together. Step 2: share or make groups.'; letter - 'Write one equation. n is the answer.'; estimate - 'Round. Estimate. Is my answer close?'. BUILD #17 (G2, PROPOSED Q11): Read it. What happens first? / Step 1: circle the sign. Solve. / Step 2: use my Step 1 answer. / Write the answer and the unit. Chant 'First this. Then that.'

Say frames (the model's Say: band, oral, never written in a cell - VQ-ONEANSWER): 'First I find ___. Then I ___.' / 'The answer is __ __.' (columns, frames); 'My equation is __. n is __.' (letter); 'About __. My answer __ is close.' (estimate); G2: 'First I add. Then I take away. I have __ __ now.'

Instruction strings (contract.js library): story-work 'Circle the sign. Write the numbers in the boxes. Solve.' (columns), story-work-ring (frames), story-rcdws (P5 lesson page); NEW strings PROPOSED Q10: 'story-letter' 'Write one equation with n. Then find n.' and 'story-estimate' 'Solve. Then estimate. Is your answer close?' (at most 8 words each).

openQuestions.q: Accept every option value, role and host decision marked PROPOSED in section 7a?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, all as proposed (Q2-Q12 below are the ones that change behaviour).

openQuestions.q: 'Within N' on a two-step story: does the band cap only the answer, or every computed number (the Step 1 result too)? Today the default deals answers to 127 (Step 1 to 145) against Max Number 100, and band 50 gives a Step 1 result of 73.
openQuestions.recommended: Every computed number (the Step 1 result and the answer) is at most N; band values 30 / 50, no band = the Max Number (100 was appended for the G2 lesson and dropped, lead ruling R2 2026-11-13: at Max Number 100 it dealt the same as no band, which the G2 lesson now takes; old B100 codes decode to no band). Rulings R-ADDSUB-*, R-BAND-* check it.

openQuestions.q: Any new preset skill under the 2026-10-17 rule (msOps mult / div alone, msChoose, wpFrames, wpBar, a G2 'two-step + and − within 100')?
openQuestions.recommended: No new preset (amended by the lead, 2026-11-13, under the owner's delegation, against the 2026-10-17 rule that a distinct option - a new representation or task kind - is ALSO a findable preset skill): the five presets stay; wpBar (a new representation) IS findable, as multi_step_word '(Visual)', which defaults to it (decision 5); msChoose stays a plain option: read in gen-algebraic.js (msChoose block), word-work.js and cells/word-work.js chooseLayout, the pupil still SOLVES the same x / ÷-first two-step story and only answers by checking one of four numbers (the answer and the three two-step errors) - a response mode on the same task, not choosing the operations (no new task kind); msOps mult / div alone are the two chunks of two_step_mult_div_first's one lesson; wpFrames is a scaffold fade; forms are the orders of one G2 lesson, whose skill is the host's default (multi_step_word, no band).

openQuestions.q: Build the two-step bar model (a new graphic: Step 1 bar - equal groups or part-whole - and Step 2 bar carrying the Step 1 answer), drawn on the teaching pages and as wpBar on practice pages? Today wpBar is offered but draws nothing on a two-step story.
openQuestions.recommended: Yes: it is IXL's 'strip models' and WDS 11.9's two-step schema; add the row 'Two-step story -> two step columns, each with its schema' to WDS 18.1 and the library entry before the build (VQ-1 says so); first build at medium.

openQuestions.q: multi_step_word '(Visual)' and multi_step_word_plain deal identical items. What makes the Visual twin visual?
openQuestions.recommended: The twin draws the two-step bar model by default (wpBar default on); _plain keeps it off. No new skill, no label change.

openQuestions.q: Print the hidden middle question (P-WP-11 v1: 'How many apples in the bags?' under Step 1) on the teaching pages?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes on Model and Guided only (a hint that fades); never on practice, test or screen practice.

openQuestions.q: two_step_letter_equation: grade the equation, or only n?
openQuestions.recommended: Both: the equation (signs and three numbers, one answer) and n are two graded answers; the skill's name is the equation.
The answer and the estimate; Yes / No is ungraded reflection that the key rings. Stay on + / − stories with 2-digit numbers (rounding to tens is meaningful); x / ÷ estimates are not added.

openQuestions.q: Capacity per page (section 3 notes) before measurement?
openQuestions.recommended: Columns S 3 / M 2 / L 2, frames S 4 / M 4 / L 2, letter and estimate S 4 / M 3 / L 2, with the bar model S 2 / M 1 / L 1 (lead ruling R1 2026-11-13 (a): measured S 2 / M 1 / L 1; a bar beside the column work cannot reach M 2 (probe, widest of 200 stories at M: bar across 132.3 x 29.8 mm, stacked 62.5 x 61.6 mm, the two step columns 107 mm wide and 53.7 mm tall, the story 27.5 mm - side by side needs 181-247 mm of a 174 mm row and a 102 mm cell, over 93 mm); M holds 1 as a ruled pin and the one-story practice page must not stretch its row (a role change, lf-roles); check ws-two-step --print CAP-BAND); the build measures and the card is resigned only if a number falls (resigned 2026-11-13 for M 2 -> 1).
Yes, as worded in section 3 (at most 8 words, the library's grammar).

openQuestions.q: Lesson data for the seven skills (prereqs.js 0/7: the lesson role falls back today). The G2 BUILD lesson #17 routine as in section 3?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes: lesson 7's routine for the x / ÷-first skills, the follow-on routines for the presets, the G2 routine for multi_step_word(_plain); the build writes them in prereqs.js.

openQuestions.q: WRM tags: the presets have none (no WRM step teaches 3.OA.D.8; lessons-6-7 open question).
openQuestions.recommended: Keep the presets untagged (site lesson linked direct, as now); tag multi_step_word(_plain) Y2.B4.S10 partial (two-step + / − without money) beside its current Y5 / Y6 tags; search terms as listed in section 7.
